title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-27
content:
2026-03-04 - scratchpad / quick ops TODOs

Morning quick notes:
- 07:30 - slack from @miguel: spikes in encoder latency for hosted-api model small-v2 in us-west1. Looks like node contention + noisy tenant jobs.
- Pager last night (INFRA-452) - autoscale didn't add capacity fast enough; need to check the scaling policy thresholds.

Top priorities for today:
- [ ] Reduce noisy-job impact on hosted pools: identify offenders, apply QoS/limits (cgroup/cpu shares or affinity)
- [ ] Triage auto-scale lag: trace from metric ingestion -> controller decision -> node provisioning (timings)
- [ ] Confirm network egress rules for new on-prem cluster (edge-runner-3) before provisioning GPUs
- [ ] Revisit GPU pool sizing for Dedicated customers: finalize new safety buffer numbers and update capacity plan doc

Notes / commands to run (quick):
- Check pool usage (k8s): kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=hosted-us-west -o wide --sort-by=.status.startTime
- Check node autoscaler events: kubectl -n kube-system describe hpa hosted-pool-autoscaler | tail -n 80
- GPU metrics (prom): sum by (pool) (gpu_utilization{env="prod"}) -> compare 01-03 vs 03-04
- Quick grep for noisy tenants: kubectl -n inference top pods --containers | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 30

Observations / hypotheses:
- During the 02:50-03:10 window we saw a high volume of small token requests; batching fell apart due to many short-lived connections (WebSocket timeouts + non-keepalive clients). Suspect client-side keepalive misconfig (customer: acme-ads).
- Autoscaler threshold currently set to 70% avg GPU util across pool; but bursts cause transient oversubscription for ~3-4m before new nodes register (image pull + provisioning). Need a warm pool / buffer for sudden bursts.

Actions (detailed):
1) Noisy-job mitigation (owner: Maya)
   - Add PodDisruptionBudget + resourceQuota for tenant namespace 'acme-ads'? Not ideal - need per-tenant QoS.
   - Plan: add LimitRange + QoS class, set cpuRequests/limits; set nodeAffinity to leverage burstable nodes for non-latency critical jobs.
   - Follow-up: create RBAC ticket for infra-runbooks to set tenant limits.

2) Autoscale troubleshooting (owner: Ethan)
   - Timeline: instrument autoscaler controller to emit decision latency metric (decision_received -> nodes_ready). Add trace id propagation to provisioning pipeline.
   - Short-term: reduce threshold from 70% -> 60% for hosted-us-west; add pre-provisioned 'burst' nodes (2x g4dn) to warm pool for peak hours 06:00-12:00 PT.
   - Long-term: investigate predictive scaling using RLQ metrics (request rate + avg seq length). See Confluence plan linked above.

3) Networking / edge-runner-3 (owner: Ravi)
   - Confirm firewall egress rules: allow TLS outbound to S3 endpoints, KMS, and control plane ip ranges. Block other outbound by default.
   - Reminder: need to add route for on-prem subnet -> nat-gw-2 (ask networking team for route propagation).

4) Dedicated capacity planning
   - Current buffer calc: average peak + 20% safety. For Dedicated customers we should consider commit-aware buffer (commit_size + 10%) rather than generic 20%.
   - Quick numbers (us-east-1): total GPUs reserved: 240; current active: 198; slack target: 240 * 0.1 = 24 GPUs -> we have ~18 spare -> short by ~6 GPUs for 10% buffer.
   - Action: propose 6 GPU hot spares for next billing cycle; update capacity plan (Confluence).

Open questions / TODOs to resolve:
- Should we move to per-tenant burst queues that can throttle at edge LB? (pros: isolates noisy tenants; cons: complexity + latency for small requests)
- How long to keep warm nodes running? Cost tradeoff for 24/7 vs. business hours only. Need finance input.
- PR #782 needs a lightweight rollout (canary 10% traffic) for the autoscaler change - coordinate with product-hosted-api team.

Misc notes / scratch (brain dump):
- Quick checklist before next oncall rotation:
   * update runbook with new autoscaler thresholds + warm pool steps
   * add Grafana dashboard for 'autoscaler_decision_latency' (create panel, alert if > 120s)
   * pre-seed images on 2 warm nodes to avoid image-pull delay (docker pull registry.redwood.ai/inf-runtime:2026-02-28)

- Slack snippets to send:
   * @product-hosted-api FYI planning an autoscaler threshold change today 10:00 PT. Will canary at 10:30 (10% traffic).
   * @finance Need quick note: adding 6 GPU hot spares in us-east-1 will increase infra commit ~ $X/month - need approval for Q2. (attach cost calc)

End-of-day goals:
- Get canary PR merged and deployed (autoscaler threshold + warm pool)
- Network rules for edge-runner-3 confirmed and staged
- Updated capacity plan with commit-aware buffer numbers and send to ops-review

Notes-to-self: keep this doc terse - move stable procedures to Confluence 'infra/runbooks' once validated.

----
History (recent entries):
- 2026-03-02: noted sudden increase in short-seq requests from integration testing; added draft patch to LB keepalive timeout.
- 2026-02-27: capacity meeting notes - flagged need for predictive scaler prototype (see INFRA-430)
